description: The bar chart illustrates the performance of two decoding strategies—Greedy and RPG (Repetition Penalty with Guidance)—applied to two variants of the CodeLlama model (7B and 34B) across four distinct code generation evaluation metrics: EGP ↑ (higher is better), TR-N ↓ (lower is better), TR-S ↓ (lower is better), and CCP ↑ (higher is better), with performance values ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 on the vertical axis. Each metric group contains four bars representing the four model-strategy combinations: Greedy (CodeLlama-7B) in blue, RPG (CodeLlama-7B) in orange, Greedy (CodeLlama-34B) in green, and RPG (CodeLlama-34B) in red-orange. For EGP ↑, RPG (CodeLlama-34B) achieves near-perfect performance (~0.99), followed by RPG (CodeLlama-7B) at ~0.89, while Greedy methods perform significantly lower (~0.60 for 34B and near 0 for 7B). In TR-N ↓, Greedy (CodeLlama-7B) performs best (~0.70), while RPG (CodeLlama-34B) performs worst (~0.40); similar trends hold for TR-S ↓, where Greedy (CodeLlama-7B) again leads (~0.69) and RPG (CodeLlama-34B) trails (~0.31). For CCP ↑, RPG (CodeLlama-34B) again dominates (~0.93), followed by RPG (CodeLlama-7B) at ~0.72, while Greedy methods score lower (~0.70 for 34B and ~0.40 for 7B). The chart visually emphasizes that RPG generally improves performance on EGP and CCP metrics, especially for the larger 34B model, while Greedy decoding can outperform RPG on repetition-related metrics (TR-N and TR-S) for the smaller 7B model.
